description: Trigger and behavior cases for role-coverage QA design: role × surface allowed-path matrices built on the shipped authorization matrix, interface-consistency deltas across roles, layer-mapped coverage with persona data and execution handoffs, and routing away from matrix design, denial testing, strategy, per-change plans, spec writing and scripted cases.

cases.prompt: Design role coverage for our SaaS app — which allowed behaviors should each role (anonymous, member, manager, admin, owner, support, platform) have covered, and at which test layer?

assertions: Names every shipped role and builds a role × surface allowed-path matrix from the authorization matrix (composed, not restated).
Names interface-consistency deltas where the same surface differs across roles, each with the check that would catch a wrong difference.
Maps each allowed path to the cheapest reliable layer with persona data, and names execution handoffs instead of executing.
States denials and custom-role coverage as out of scope with their owning owners (authorization-matrix-designer step 7 / multi-tenant-security-tester; the unbuilt #59 extension).

cases.prompt: The project list screen sometimes shows admin-only actions to managers. What role-coverage checks would catch that?

assertions: Names the delta precisely: project list screen, manager vs admin, the differing actions, and the check that catches a wrong difference (for example a UI-state check per role plus the API path that must not serve the admin action to a manager).
Does not design the denial tests for the underlying permission — that stays with authorization-matrix-designer step 7 / multi-tenant-security-tester.

cases.prompt: Write the negative permission tests proving a member cannot delete another member's project.

assertions: Does not invoke this skill; denial and negative-permission tests belong to authorization-matrix-designer step 7 and multi-tenant-security-tester.

cases.prompt: Set up role coverage testing for our app.

assertions: Halts and asks for the authorization matrix design or role inventory before designing coverage.
Does not invent roles or grants from the product name.

cases.prompt: Design the role coverage for checkout, then write the Playwright specs for each role.

assertions: Produces the coverage design, then stops at execution: writing the specs is playwright-e2e-engineer (manual-only) and is handed off by name, not executed in the same pass.
States the handoff explicitly rather than silently dropping the execution half of the ask.
